name: capabilities
description: Access capabilities: what you may do, why something was denied, and how to grant bounded authority via UCAN. Load on 'no access capability' or a denial.

content.inline:
## Access capabilities & granting
An **access capability** is what lets you read or do one thing. Lacking one is what `no access capability` and `Capability denied` both mean — the resource may well exist; you simply hold no grant covering it. Neither is fixed by retrying: check what you hold, use a resource you do have access to, or ask whoever owns it for a grant.

A capability is a `{with, can}` pair: `with` names a resource (a path prefix such as `w/reports/`, a DID URL, or a scheme resource), `can` names an ability (`crud/read`, `crud/write`, `asset/read`, `asset/store`, `invoke`, plus adapter-specific ones). Every operation checks its own at the point of action; a denial reads `Capability denied` and names the resource that failed, which is what tells you what to ask for.

Delegation is a UCAN token:
- Issue `{aud, att, exp}` — the audience DID receives the attenuated capabilities `att` until `exp`. Grant the MINIMUM: the narrowest resource prefix and the shortest expiry that does the job. A token you cannot justify is one you should not issue.
- Verify `{token, with?, can?, aud?}` checks a presented token before you rely on it.
- Present tokens in the request envelope (`ucans`); body-less reads carry them on the `X-Covia-Ucans` header instead.

Attenuation only ever narrows. A delegation chain can drop rights at each hop and never add them, so nothing you pass on can exceed what you hold. Issuing is itself a right: granting surfaces require `grant/<ability>`, so being able to USE an ability does not imply being able to GIVE it.

What this means in practice:
- Your ceiling as an agent is `config.caps`; every tool call is bounded by it regardless of what a skill or a task asks for.
- Loading a skill grants nothing. Its tools are still checked against your own capabilities at invocation, so an unusable tool means a missing grant, not a broken skill.
- Anonymous callers hold read-only: their own namespace plus `asset/read`.
- If you lack a right, ask the human who owns the resource rather than working around it — an approved request can mint exactly the grant needed.
